_comment: Atlas Growth :: foundation repair, 10 states + 3 border metros. Engine config for google-maps-scrape. Job-specific values live ONLY here — never edit an engine script to tune this run.

qualify_rules._r: 1. Must-drop entity types. deny matches the PRIMARY google_type by default, which is what we want here: a foundation firm carrying an incidental secondary tag should survive, but a business whose PRIMARY identity is one of these is not the ICP.
qualify_rules.label: off_icp_type

qualify_rules._r: 2. Must-drop by NAME (exact, always fires regardless of primary/secondary type). Covers this vertical's three traps: collision shops answering 'structural repair', charitable foundations answering 'foundation', and restoration/pest franchises answering the waterproofing + crawl-space queries.
qualify_rules.label: name_deny

qualify_rules._r: 3. Positive allow on google_types-ANY (never primary_type — Google mis-primaries real firms; a 'Contractor | Foundation' must survive). NOTE the deliberate absence of a bare 'concrete contractor', 'contractor', 'construction company' and 'general contractor': in the Houston calibration call 79/150 records for 'foundation repair' were typed Concrete contractor, most of them flatwork. Allowing those buckets floods the list. They are recovered instead by recover-generic-config.json, which pairs the generic type WITH a foundation/leveling NAME token.
qualify_rules.label: not_in_icp

qualify_rules._r: 4. Size floor. Residential foundation repair is CONSUMER-facing, so review volume genuinely tracks size (the engine reserves review floors for exactly this case and forbids them for B2B ICPs). Set to 30 at GATE 3 (was 50 at GATE 1): Measured on the real partial run: the 30-49 review band adds 310 rows of which 292 (94%) are claimed + websited + rating>=4 - statistically indistinguishable from the kept set on EVERY free Maps signal. So the floor was never the quality gate; it is a pure volume dial. Hard qualification moved to the site-text fit gate (business_type, STEP 5e). Deliberately aggressive - the Maps floor is a SIZE gate only; real fit is judged from site_text plus the Clay pass downstream. RISK: review counts run lower in sparse states (KS/MS/AR), so a flat 50 cuts harder there. Check per-state counts at GATE 3 and, if a state is starved, run a zero-cost recovery pass at a lower floor scoped by city token, not a re-scrape.
qualify_rules.label: too_small

_no_website_rule: Deliberately NO {website, exists} rule, unlike the schema example in SKILL STEP 3. collapse-domains.js (STEP 5c-dom) classifies website as site/shared_host/none AFTER the geo gate and dedupe, so every row — including the no-website and Facebook-only ones — passes through the category and name denies first. This structurally fixes SKILL 5d gotcha (b) (a blocklisted chain riding in via the recovery track) instead of patching it with a re-qualify at the end.
_no_gov_deny: Deliberately NO government deny. The engine's standing gov deny is for distress/institutional-intent verticals ('IRS tax help', 'tax debt relief') whose queries surface public bodies. None of these 10 queries do. The charity risk that DOES exist here — a non-profit named '<X> Foundation' — is handled by the non-profit/charity type deny plus the name deny above.

brand_families._r: Verified against the web 2026-09-11. Groundworks (Cortec/Kohlberg) trades under regional OPERATING brands, not its own name, so the brand name is what appears on Maps — those are listed individually. Matching is a lowercase substring test against '<name> <root_domain>', so every term must be distinctive enough not to false-match an independent. KNOWN GAP: Trivest's 'Foundation Repair Services' platform is deliberately absent — that phrase occurs inside ordinary independent names ('Smith Foundation Repair Services LLC') and would mislabel them. A wrong brand label is worse than none; raise it at GATE 3 if the domain can be pinned down.

owner_query._r: use_linkedin false: LinkedIn is a weak rung for owner-operator residential trades and doubles SERP cost (engine note, LH trade-vertical validation). Moot this run — no SERP vendor, site_text only.
